fixture: tests/fixtures/text-geometry.ts: deterministic Helvetica PDF, 600 by 800 points, text at (100,500), optional CropBox [50,100,550,700] and page rotation
verification: tests/highlight-geometry.browser.test.tsx: eight comparisons against PDF.js raster glyph bounds (1-pixel antialiasing tolerance), one column-gutter check, and one strict comparison against an actual PDF.js TextLayer DOM Range (less than 1 CSS pixel); no mocked extraction

columnGutter.baseline: Highlight crosses blank x=250 gutter between LEFT at x=100 and RIGHT at x=400
columnGutter.improved: No returned rectangle crosses the gutter; whitespace still counts toward search offsets

proportionalGlyphWidths.reference: Actual PDF.js TextLayer DOM Range for the first four characters; native Helvetica advances are recorded separately from a second PDF containing only iiii
proportionalGlyphWidths.equalCharacterWidthControl: The previous equal-character estimate differs from the actual TextLayer range by more than 20 CSS pixels in the regression fixture
proportionalGlyphWidths.portabilityCorrection: The original less-than-1-point assertion against native Helvetica advances failed on Linux Firefox and WebKit. The strict oracle now checks actual selectable text geometry; native-font agreement is explicitly platform-dependent. No production measurement code or tolerance was changed.

limitations: This fixes search highlight geometry; it does not alter PDF text extraction, search normalization, selection ordering, or hyphenation.

Partial glyph widths follow PDF.js selectable text-layer fallback-font measurement scaled to the PDF run width. Fallback glyph proportions vary by platform: native Helvetica advance discrepancy was about 0.013 points on macOS and 2.70 points on Linux Firefox/WebKit for this fixture. This does not establish exact agreement with native PDF glyphs, complex shaping, or mixed-direction runs.
Vertical-writing direction and pure RTL geometry additionally have streamed-item regression coverage; the generated PDF fixture uses horizontal Helvetica.
